title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: Set on the desert planet Arrakis, Dune is the story of the boy Paul Atreides, heir to a noble family tasked with ruling an inhospitable world where the only thing of value is the spice melange, a drug capable of extending life and enhancing consciousness.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: Ryland Grace is the sole survivor on a desperate, last-chance mission—and if he fails, humanity and the earth itself are doomed. Except right now, he doesn't know that. He can't even remember his own name, let alone the nature of his assignment or how to complete it.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
description: Case was the sharpest data-thief in the matrix—until he crossed the wrong people and they crippled his nervous system. Now a mysterious employer recruits him for a last-chance run against an unthinkably powerful artificial intelligence.

title: Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
description: For twelve thousand years the Galactic Empire has ruled supreme. Now it is dying. But only Hari Seldon, creator of the revolutionary science of psychohistory, can see into the future—to a dark age of ignorance and barbarism that will last thirty thousand years.

title: The Three-Body Problem
author: Cixin Liu
description: Set against the backdrop of China's Cultural Revolution, a secret military project sends signals into space to establish contact with aliens. An alien civilization on the brink of destruction captures the signal and plans to invade Earth.

title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
author: Robert C. Martin
description: Even bad code can function. But if code isn't clean, it can bring a development organization to its knees. Every year, countless hours and significant resources are lost because of poorly written code. This book teaches the values and practices of software craftsmanship.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: Data is at the center of many challenges in system design today. Difficult issues need to be figured out, such as scalability, consistency, reliability, efficiency, and maintainability. This book provides a comprehensive guide through the principles and practicalities of modern data architectures.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: Andrew Hunt, David Thomas
description: The Pragmatic Programmer cuts through the increasing specialization and technicalities of modern software development to examine the core process—taking a requirement and producing working, maintainable code that delights its users.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: No matter your goals, Atomic Habits offers a proven framework for improving—every day. James Clear, one of the world's leading experts on habit formation, reveals practical strategies that will teach you exactly how to form good habits, break bad ones, and master tiny behaviors.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: In the international bestseller, Thinking, Fast and Slow, Daniel Kahneman, the renowned psychologist and winner of the Nobel Prize in Economics, takes us on a groundbreaking tour of the mind and explains the two systems that drive the way we think.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: From a renowned historian comes a groundbreaking narrative of humanity’s creation and evolution—a #1 international bestseller—that explores the ways in which biology and history have defined us and enhanced our understanding of what it means to be human.

author: George Orwell
description: Winston Smith toes the Party line, rewriting history to satisfy the Ministry of Truth. With each lie he writes, Winston grows to hate the Party that seeks power for its own sake and persecutes those who dare to commit thoughtcrimes.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: The Great Gatsby, F. Scott Fitzgerald's third book, stands as the supreme achievement of his career. This exemplary novel of the Jazz Age has been acclaimed by generations of readers.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: The unforgettable novel of a childhood in a sleepy Southern town and the crisis of conscience that rocked it, To Kill A Mockingbird became an instant bestseller and a critical success when it was first published in 1960.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
description: Alicia Berenson’s life is seemingly perfect. A famous painter married to an in-demand fashion photographer, she lives in a grand house overlooking a park in one of London’s most desirable areas. One evening, she shoots her husband five times in the face and never speaks another word.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
description: On a warm summer morning in North Carthage, Missouri, it is Nick and Amy Dunne’s fifth wedding anniversary. Presents are being wrapped and reservations are being made when Nick’s clever and beautiful wife disappears from their rented pine house.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
description: Ten strangers are lured to an isolated island mansion off the Devon coast by a mysterious host. One by one, the guests share the darkest secrets of their wicked pasts. And one by one, they die.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: Bilbo Baggins is a hobbit who enjoys a comfortable, unambitious life, rarely traveling any farther than his pantry or cellar. But his contentment is disturbed when the wizard Gandalf and a company of dwarves arrive on his doorstep one day to whisk him away on an adventure.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: Told in Kvothe's own voice, this is the tale of the magically gifted young man who grows to be the most notorious wizard his world has ever seen. The intimate screen of his childhood in a troupe of traveling players, his years spent as a near-feral orphan in a crime-riddled city, his daringly brazen attempt to enter a legendary school of magic.

title: A Game of Thrones
author: George R.R. Martin
description: Long ago, in a time forgotten, a preternatural event threw the seasons out of balance. In a land where summers can last decades and winters a lifetime, trouble is brewing. The cold is returning, and in the frozen wastes to the north of Winterfell, sinister and supernatural forces are massing.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
description: Few ancient works have been as influential as the Meditations of Marcus Aurelius, Roman emperor from A.D. 161 to 180. A series of spiritual exercises filled with wisdom, practical guidance, and profound understanding of human behavior, it remains one of the greatest works of spiritual and ethical reflection ever written.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
description: Psychiatrist Viktor Frankl's memoir has riveted generations of readers with its descriptions of life in Nazi death camps and its lessons for spiritual survival. Frankl argues that we cannot avoid suffering, but we can choose how to cope with it, find meaning in it, and move forward with renewed purpose.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
description: Born to survivalists in the mountains of Idaho, Tara Westover was seventeen the first time she set foot in a classroom. Her family was so isolated from mainstream society that there was no one to ensure the children received an education, and no one to intervene when an older brother became violent.

title: Steve Jobs
author: Walter Isaacson
description: Based on more than forty interviews with Steve Jobs conducted over two years—as well as interviews with more than a hundred family members, friends, adversaries, competitors, and colleagues—Walter Isaacson has written a riveting story of the roller-coaster life and searingly intense personality of a creative entrepreneur.

title: Let Us C
author: Yashavant Kanetkar
description: The iconic, universally acclaimed guide to learning C programming in Indian engineering colleges. Renowned for its lucid explanations of pointer arithmetic, dynamic memory allocation, console graphics, recursion, bitwise operators, and structured programming fundamentals.

title: Programming in ANSI C
author: E. Balagurusamy
description: The quintessential introductory programming textbook across Indian university syllabi. Offers step-by-step guidance on algorithmic problem solving, structured flowcharts, arrays, user-defined functions, structures, unions, and file input/output in C.

title: The C Programming Language
author: Brian W. Kernighan, Dennis M. Ritchie
description: The classic 'K&R' reference manual authored by the creators of the C language. A masterclass in concise technical writing covering memory models, pointers, bit manipulation, and the standard UNIX system library interface.

title: Object-Oriented Programming with C++
author: E. Balagurusamy
description: A prescribed staple across B.Tech computer science and IT curricula. Introduces object-oriented programming concepts including classes, objects, data abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, virtual functions, templates, and exception handling in C++.

title: The C++ Programming Language
author: Bjarne Stroustrup
description: Written by the inventor of C++, this definitive masterwork details modern language features, standard template library (STL), generic algorithms, resource management via RAII, and concurrent programming.

title: Java: The Complete Reference
author: Herbert Schildt
description: The definitive guide to Java programming. Covers the entire Java syntax, object-oriented design principles, Java Virtual Machine internals, multithreaded programming, generics, lambda expressions, and the Java Collections Framework.

title: Core Java: An Integrated Approach
author: R. Nageswara Rao
description: A comprehensive reference written with university exams and technical placement interviews in mind. Covers Core Java, AWT, Swing, multithreading, JDBC connectivity, and collection frameworks with extensive code examples.

title: Python Crash Course: A Hands-On, Project-Based Introduction
author: Eric Matthes
description: A best-selling, thorough guide to Python programming. The first half covers fundamental concepts such as data structures, functions, classes, and file handling; the second half walks through practical real-world projects in web development, data visualization, and game creation.

title: Programming Python: Powerful Object-Oriented Programming
author: Mark Lutz
description: An exhaustive reference on advanced Python programming techniques. Emphasizes real-world application domains including GUI development, network protocol integration, systems administration scripting, and enterprise database integration.

title: JavaScript: The Definitive Guide
author: David Flanagan
description: Known as the definitive 'Rhino Book', this comprehensive manual covers modern ECMAScript standards, closures, prototypes, asynchronous promises, async/await, Document Object Model (DOM), Node.js, and web APIs.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms in C
author: Reema Thareja
description: Widely regarded as the standard textbook for Data Structures across Indian engineering colleges. Details arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, sorting algorithms, searching mechanisms, and algorithmic complexity with step-by-step C implementations.

title: Data Structures Using C and C++
author: Yedidyah Langsam, Moshe J. Augenstein, Aaron M. Tenenbaum
description: The time-tested foundational textbook on data representation, dynamic memory management, recursion, binary search trees, B-trees, graph traversals, and hashing techniques.

title: Introduction to Algorithms (CLRS)
author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein
description: The internationally acclaimed authority on algorithms. Combines mathematical rigor with comprehensive analysis of sorting algorithms, advanced data structures, graph theory, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, and NP-completeness.

title: Database System Concepts
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth, S. Sudarshan
description: The cornerstone textbook for database management systems across universities worldwide. Covers the relational model, SQL queries, entity-relationship schemas, normalization theory (1NF through BCNF), transaction processing, concurrency control, and recovery.

title: Operating System Concepts
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin, Greg Gagne
description: Widely known as the 'Dinosaur Book', this classic offers an in-depth treatment of operating system design, processes and threads, CPU scheduling algorithms, mutual exclusion and deadlocks, memory management, virtual memory paging, and storage architectures.

title: Computer Networks
author: Andrew S. Tanenbaum, David J. Wetherall
description: The gold standard textbook on computer networking. Explores networking architectures from the physical layer up to the application layer, covering fiber optics, data link protocols, IP routing algorithms, TCP congestion control, and network security.

title: Data Communications and Networking
author: Behrouz A. Forouzan
description: Celebrated for its intuitive, visual diagrams and pedagogical approach. Thoroughly explains signal transmission, digital modulation, error detection and correction, subnetting, IPv4/IPv6 architectures, and socket programming.

title: Computer System Architecture
author: M. Morris Mano
description: The quintessential engineering textbook detailing digital hardware organization, register transfer micro-operations, central processing unit control design, pipelining, memory hierarchy, and input/output asynchronous data transfer.

title: Digital Logic and Computer Design
author: M. Morris Mano
description: The classic foundational book for digital electronics and computer hardware engineering. Covers Boolean algebra, Karnaugh mapping, logic gate simplification, combinational circuits (adders, multiplexers, decoders), and sequential flip-flop counters.

title: Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach
author: Roger S. Pressman, Bruce R. Maxim
description: The world's foremost authority on professional software engineering practices. Covers agile methodologies, software process models, requirement engineering, UML architectural design, software testing suites, and project metrics.

title: Theory of Computer Science: Automata, Languages and Computation
author: K.L.P. Mishra, N. Chandrasekaran
description: A prescribed guide in Indian universities for automata theory, regular expressions, finite state automata, context-free grammars, pushdown automata, Turing machines, and Chomsky hierarchy of languages.

title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools
author: Alfred V. Aho, Monica S. Lam, Ravi Sethi, Jeffrey D. Ullman
description: Universally known as the 'Dragon Book', this is the defining work on compiler construction, lexical analyzers (Lex), syntax parsers (Yacc/Bison), syntax-directed translation, intermediate code generation, and compiler optimization.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
author: Stuart Russell, Peter Norvig
description: The premier global textbook on artificial intelligence. Examines rational agents, search algorithms (A*, minimax), constraint satisfaction, knowledge representation, probabilistic inference, deep learning architectures, and natural language processing.

title: Cryptography and Network Security: Principles and Practice
author: William Stallings
description: An authoritative guide to cybersecurity engineering. Covers symmetric key ciphers (DES, AES), public-key cryptography (RSA, ECC), cryptographic hash functions, digital signatures, IPSec, TLS/SSL, and malicious software defense mechanisms.

title: Web Technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP
author: Uttam K. Roy
description: The standard B.Tech university text for Web Technologies. Explains HTML5, CSS3, DOM scripting with JavaScript, XML, server-side programming using PHP, and MySQL database connectivity with hands-on lab exercises.

title: Higher Engineering Mathematics
author: B.S. Grewal
description: The legendary, most widely issued textbook in Indian engineering college libraries. A comprehensive masterwork covering linear algebra, differential and integral calculus, vector calculus, ordinary and partial differential equations, Fourier series, Laplace transforms, and numerical analysis.

title: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering
author: V.K. Mehta, Rohit Mehta
description: Essential first-year engineering textbook explaining DC and AC circuit theory, electromagnetic induction, single-phase and three-phase transformers, semiconductor diodes, bipolar junction transistors, and operational amplifiers.

title: Cloud Computing: Concepts, Technology & Architecture
author: Thomas Erl, Ricardo Puttini, Zaigham Mahmood
description: Authoritative reference text on cloud computing architecture, infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), PaaS, SaaS, containerization, hypervisors, multitenancy, cloud storage mechanisms, and distributed resiliency.
